title: Relative cotangent criterion for surjectivity of complete local maps
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $C,R,S$ be complete Noetherian local commutative $k$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], all with specified residue field $k$. Here a local ring has a unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$; complete means complete for the powers of that ideal. Let $C\to R$, $C\to S$ and $f:R\to S$ be continuous local $k$-algebra homomorphisms inducing the identity on $k$, with $f$ compatible with the two maps from $C$. Write $\mathfrak m_CR$ and $\mathfrak m_CS$ for the ideals generated by the images of $\mathfrak m_C$. Then $f$ is surjective if and only if its induced $k$-linear map $\mathfrak m_R/(\mathfrak m_CR+\mathfrak m_R^2)\to\mathfrak m_S/(\mathfrak m_CS+\mathfrak m_S^2)$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 06GZ (lemma-surjective-cotangent-space), equivalence (1) and (3), with coefficient base Lambda=C and common residue field k.

proof.text: If $f$ is surjective, any $s\in\mathfrak m_S$ has a preimage $r\in R$. Since the residue map of $f$ is the identity on $k$, the residue of $r$ is zero, so $r\in\mathfrak m_R$. Passing to the indicated quotients gives the required surjective relative cotangent map. Locality and compatibility with $C$ ensure that this quotient map is well defined.

source.place: Tag 06GZ (lemma-surjective-cotangent-space), equivalence (1) and (3); relative-to-absolute cotangent argument in lemma-surjective; complete-source lifting supplied by the cited Mathlib node.

proof.text: Conversely assume relative cotangent surjectivity. For $s\in\mathfrak m_S$, choose $r\in\mathfrak m_R$ such that $s-f(r)\in\mathfrak m_CS+\mathfrak m_S^2$, and write its first summand as $\sum_i c_i s_i$ with $c_i$ the image of an element of $\mathfrak m_C$. Choose $\lambda_i\in k$ equal to the residue of $s_i$. Then $c_i(s_i-\lambda_i)\in\mathfrak m_S^2$, and $\sum_i c_i\lambda_i$ is the image under $f$ of an element of $\mathfrak m_R$, by $C$-compatibility and $k$-linearity. Thus $\mathfrak m_S=f(\mathfrak m_R)+\mathfrak m_S^2$ as additive subgroups. In particular, for $J=\mathfrak m_RS$ one has $\mathfrak m_S=J+\mathfrak m_S^2$ and $J\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$.

source.place: Tag 06GZ (lemma-surjective-cotangent-space), equivalence (1) and (3); relative-to-absolute cotangent argument in lemma-surjective; complete-source lifting supplied by the cited Mathlib node.

proof.text: Apply Nakayama to the $S$-module $M=\mathfrak m_S/J$ and the ideal $\mathfrak m_S$. The maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_S$ is finitely generated because $S$ is Noetherian, and the images of those generators generate $M$. The preceding equality gives $\mathfrak m_SM=(\mathfrak m_S^2+J)/J=M$. Since $S$ has exactly one maximal ideal, $\mathfrak m_S$ is its Jacobson radical. The cited Nakayama statement gives $M=0$, hence $J=\mathfrak m_S$.

source.place: Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK), part (2), applied to the quotient module of the maximal ideal.

proof.text: Use the complete-source surjectivity lemma with $I=\mathfrak m_R$. Completeness of $R$ supplies $I$-adic precompleteness. By $IS=J=\mathfrak m_S$, completeness of $S$ supplies $IS$-adic Hausdorffness: an element in every $\mathfrak m_S^n$ maps to zero in the inverse limit, so is zero by injectivity of the completion map. Finally $R\to S/IS=S/\mathfrak m_S=k$ is surjective because the residue map is the identity on $k$. All hypotheses of the cited lemma hold, so $f$ is surjective.

lean.note: Relative cotangent-map surjectivity is expanded exactly on representatives: for every s in m_S there is r in m_R with f(r)-s in m_C S + m_S^2. This is equivalent to surjectivity of the canonical map on the stated quotients; the map is not an arbitrary parameter.
